messages:
anya-peopleops: Heads up team — Leon (new SWE) just told us his dependent consular appointment got rescheduled and that may delay his visa stamping by ~2 weeks. His original offer start date is June 1. Need options for start/payroll/benefits and whether we can ship equipment internationally.

miguel-peopleops: Thanks. First thing: does Leon currently have any US work authorization (H-1B stamped, I-797 COS, EAD)? Payroll depends on that.

leon-newhire: Hi all, I have an approved I-797 for COS but I left the US for family reasons and now need a consular stamp to return. No stamp yet. Really sorry for the timing.

immigration-legal: If he is outside the US without a stamp, he cannot lawfully work for us until he re-enters with the proper visa. If he is inside the US with I-797, we can proceed normally. For someone outside the US we cannot start payroll. We can consider limited unpaid onboarding.

sara-finance: To reiterate, benefits enrollment is tied to active payroll. If we delay payroll, health/dental won't start until his first paid cycle. We can, however, process relocation reimbursements earlier if Finance receives receipts and approvals.

anya-peopleops: Options to present to Leon: (1) Move official start date to after he has stamped and returned. (2) Allow voluntary unpaid onboarding (training, account setup) prior to payroll start. (3) Explore temporary paid contractor route — legal + finance must sign off; typically not preferred for COS cases.

naveen-eng: Manager perspective: we want Leon to start team ramp asap. For unpaid onboarding, we'd still like to give him access to docs and asynchronous training. Can IT ship a laptop to his local address (outside US)?

it-ops-bot: IT checklist: international laptop shipments require manager sign-off, shipping address confirmation, customs paperwork, and signed asset acceptance. We can ship to Mexico/Canada/EU in 5-12 business days depending on carrier. Note: we cannot ship some cryptographic dongles to certain countries without compliance approval.

miguel-peopleops: Good detail. We should also flag equity/legal timing: vesting schedule and equity grant effective date are tied to the official start. We can request an exception but need CEO and People Ops approval.

anya-peopleops: I'll draft a concise candidate email that outlines the unpaid onboarding option and the documents required when he arrives. Also drafting a short consulate note the manager can print if Leon wants it to support family appointment scheduling.

immigration-legal: Suggested wording for consulate note: keep it factual and avoid implying payroll or prior employment. Example paragraph: "Redwood Inference confirms an offer of employment to Leon Garcia for the position of Software Engineer with an intended start date of June 1, 2026. Due to an unexpected rescheduling of a dependent consular appointment, the applicant requires a visa stamping appointment. We respectfully request any available appointment accommodations to enable timely completion of required formalities."

anya-peopleops: Candidate checklist (for Leon / manager) — copying into the thread so Miguel can forward: 
```
For unpaid onboarding (no payroll):
- Manager approval for unpaid/voluntary onboarding (email confirmation)
- Signed offer letter, NDA, and any preboarding paperwork
- IT asset request + shipping address + signed asset acknowledgement
- Access to documentation, recorded onboarding sessions, and non-billable training
- No client-facing or revenue-generating tasks until visa stamped and payroll starts

To begin paid employment (employee physically in US):
- Passport with valid visa stamp OR I-797 showing COS if already in US
- Completed I-9 documentation presented in-person (List A or combination per policy)
- Direct deposit form and payroll forms completed
- Proof of US residential address for tax withholding
```

anya-peopleops: Finance note: if Leon provides receipts for flights or urgent relocation costs, Finance can process reimbursements prior to payroll in exceptional cases. Sara, can you confirm threshold and timeline?

sara-finance: We can reimburse up to $2,000 for urgent reloc/visa costs prior to payroll with manager + People Ops approval and receipts. Payments processed as reimbursable expense within 7-10 business days after submission.

immigration-legal: Contractor route note: We generally avoid classifying incoming COS candidates as contractors because it raises compliance and immigration exposure. If the candidate insists on interim paid work, we'll prepare a short memo outlining legal risk and controls, but we do not recommend it as first option.

miguel-peopleops: Proposed action items: 1) Miguel to email Leon with the unpaid onboarding offer + checklist today. 2) IT to estimate shipping time & customs for Leon's country (if manager requests laptop). 3) Legal to deliver contractor risk memo by EOD tomorrow if Leon asks about paid interim. 4) Finance prepared to expedite reimbursements if needed.

it-ops-bot: IT: please provide carrier ETA and any prohibited item concerns for shipments to the candidate's country.

leon-newhire: Thanks team. I'll opt for unpaid onboarding and would appreciate the laptop shipped if shipping is permitted. I'll send my preferred address and sign the asset ack now.

anya-peopleops: Great. Miguel, please loop Leon into a Google doc with the checklist and attach the consulate template. We'll reconvene if the appointment date changes. :white_check_mark:
